Who We Are
Atlan is building the context layer for enterprise AI. Enterprises are pouring money into AI and most of it dies in production because the AI does not understand the business context around the data. That is the problem Atlan solves.

Gartner has named context the defining issue in enterprise AI, and calls context graphs the essential infrastructure for AI agents, naming Atlan one of three vendors already building it. We are also the only vendor named a Leader across all four major Gartner and Forrester evaluations for data catalogs, data governance and metadata management, the foundation the context layer runs on.
Come build the infrastructure that AI runs on.
Who We Are
Gartner calls context the defining issue in enterprise AI, and context graphs the essential infrastructure for AI agents. It names Atlan as one of three vendors already building one. We're also the only vendor named a Leader in all four major Gartner and Forrester evaluations for data catalogs, data governance and metadata management, the layer our context graph is built on.
Come build the infrastructure AI runs on.

The Team
You'll join the team building Atlan's context layer, the platforms that make it possible and the vertical agents that run on it. The platform is what any agent needs before an enterprise will trust it: a registry of which agents and skills exist, traces and evals on every run, and governance over cost and access.
Vertical agents each do one specific job, for customers and for Atlan's own teams. Inside Atlan they already run real work. There's an agent our CSMs trust, three GTM agents that replace 3,000 calls made by hand, an agent that watches every page on atlan.com, and one that monitors the other agents. We write up what we learn in the open at Becoming Frontier.
The team works in small "two-slice" units. You own one initiative, usually with one or two people alongside you, and you decide how it gets built.

What will you do?
You'll take problems nobody has fully defined yet and ship working systems, fast. Depending on where you're matched, you may:
• 
Own a 0→1 initiative from problem to production. Frame it, write the spec when there isn't one, pick the architecture and build it.
• 
Build agents with the people who own the outcome, inside Atlan or at a customer. Scope the workflow with them, demo early and put the agent where the work already happens, like an approval in Slack or a redline in a legal team's Word doc.
• 
Earn autonomy with evidence. Start with shadow runs, study the misses and widen what the agent can do as results support it.
• 
Design for failure. Decide what happens when a tool is down, context is thin or the agent isn't sure, and how a person takes over.
• 
Make the engineering calls on what stays deterministic code and what needs a model, build vs. reuse, model choice, cost and reliability. Explain the trade-offs clearly.
• 
Make agent behavior observable. Tie traces and evals to the revision that ran. Track consistency, cost and latency alongside success rate, and treat drift as a regression.
• 
Build on and extend the context layer, agent platform and registry: versioned skills, layered instructions, explicit permissions for tools and secrets, and model changes handled as migrations with evals rerun before promotion.
• 
Build AI-native yourself. Run coding agents on your own work, keep their skills and instructions up to date, and review what they write for architectural drift.
• 
Share what you learn. Turn what works into skills, reference architectures and quality gates that others adopt, and demo what you've built.
What makes you a great match for us?
Must have
• 
You've built software systems hands-on and shipped 0→1 products or platforms into production, often without a spec.
• 
You've shipped agents or LLM systems that real people use. When one went wrong, you traced it back to the context, tool call or decision that caused it.
• 
You use evals to find and fix real problems, check what a score actually counts, and judge agents by user impact: hours saved, error rate or cycle time.
• 
You design for failure first: what the agent may touch, what happens when it's wrong, and where a person approves before it acts.
• 
You build with coding agents every day and hold what they write to the same bar as your own code.
• 
You're a critical optimist. You believe what agents can do is real, and test what still fails before trusting them with more.
• 
You reason from first principles. When a familiar design doesn't fit, or a better model makes old scaffolding unnecessary, you notice and rebuild.
• 
You have strong systems judgment. You can design for production reliability, latency, cost and security, build it yourself, and leave it in a shape others can build on.
• 
You do your best work owning an initiative with one or two people alongside you, and don't need a large team to feel effective.
Strong bonus
• 
Experience with MCP, A2A, agent frameworks and runtimes, LLM gateways or agent observability, or you've built an agent harness or orchestration layer yourself.
• 
Experience with knowledge graphs, vector search, retrieval or semantic layers.
• 
You've built an eval suite from scratch, or run shadow evaluations, LLM grading or staged rollouts.
• 
You've shipped agents that write to a system of record, with permissions, approvals and an audit trail.
• 
You've led AI adoption inside an engineering or business team and can show the before and after.
• 
Founding-engineer, technical-founder or early-stage startup experience, where you built something from nothing.
• 
A public trail of work, repos, demos, write-ups or talks, that shows how you build.
This role probably isn't for you if you want to manage a large team, want a well-scoped backlog handed to you, would rather build demos than run agents in production, or are still planning to get into AI.

Why Atlan?
Joining Atlan means being part of a global movement to help data teams do their life’s best work. Here’s what you can expect:
• 
Competitive Compensation: We benchmark at the top of the market and keep compensation simple: strong base salary, performance‑based variable pay, and impact‑driven equity (for most roles), so your total rewards grow in step with the value you create over time.
• 
AI Native Culture: Atlan is where AI-native builders come to build the systems the future of work will run on. AI isn’t an add-on, it’s woven into how we build, think, and work every day, empowering every Atlanian to move faster and create a bigger impact.
• 
Health & Wellness: From Day‑1 health, dental, vision, and mental health to flexible health stipends, we design benefits offerings that lead in each country we're in.
• 
Flexible Time Off & Leave Policies: We trust you to own your energy: flexible time off and modern leave so you can unplug properly, support yourself and your loved ones, and come back ready to drive an impact.
• 
Accelerated Growth & Learning: Develop at an uncommon velocity through cutting-edge tech, complex implementations, and an experienced team that values mastery.
• 
Global, Remote-First, High-Trust: Work from anywhere with a diverse team across 15+ countries, in a trust-first, async environment that gives you true flexibility and ownership over how you work.

More About Us
Atlan is building the shared context layer that enterprises need so AI can operate on trusted, governed context. The conversation has moved from data leaders asking: “Can we trust the data in our stack?” to businesses asking: “Can we trust AI inside the business?”
We are the missing infrastructure for businesses becoming AI-forward - the connective tissue between their data stack, operational systems, and AI agents.

To learn more, visit www.atlan.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

About the team
Sarvam builds Indic-language AI used at population scale. The CPU Infrastructure team runs everything outside the GPU fleet: Kubernetes across Azure, AWS, GCP and Indian sovereign clouds, the network between them, Cloudflare, identity, secrets, observability, cost and the delivery pipeline every product ships through.
The team builds and runs what it builds. Engineers own real systems end to end, and every repeated piece of manual work is a candidate for automation. As an AI company, we are building AI agents into our own operations, to plan and review infrastructure changes, triage alerts and handle routine issues, with engineers setting the guardrails.
About the role
You are an infrastructure engineer whose first instinct is security, and who builds rather than only operates. You have worked on banking, fintech, payments or similarly regulated products, where a misconfiguration is an incident and an audit is routine. Here you set what “secure” means across Sarvam’s infrastructure and build the automation that enforces it, so security is a property of the pipeline rather than a review step. You work closely with the compliance team.
This is a hands-on role: most of your time goes into building, and you guide engineering teams across Sarvam on security — setting standards, reviewing security-relevant work and mentoring engineers.
Responsibilities
• Define and enforce security baselines for Kubernetes, cloud accounts, container images and CI/CD across all clouds
• Write the policy gates in the delivery pipeline (OPA / Conftest, Kyverno or equivalent): network exposure, IAM, image provenance, secrets, data residency
• Own secrets and workload identity: Vault or cloud-native equivalents, rotation, short-lived and scoped credentials, no long-lived keys
• Build detection and response: runtime security (Falco / Tetragon or equivalent), log-based detections, alerting and playbooks
• Run the finding-to-fix loop for security findings: triage, assign, fix, add a detection, retest
• Use LLMs and AI agents in security work: triaging findings, reviewing infrastructure changes, tuning detections, drafting incident timelines — and secure the agents themselves with scoped, short-lived permissions and audit trails
• Harden the supply chain: image signing and scanning, dependency policy, SBOMs
• Automate compliance evidence (CERT-In, ISO 27001, SOC 2, DPDP) together with the compliance team
• Set the security standards other engineers follow and review security-relevant changes
• Take part in on-call and lead security incidents
Requirements
• 5–9 years in DevOps, platform or security engineering, with at least 2 in a bank, fintech, payments company or other regulated environment
• Strong Kubernetes and Linux fundamentals; has run production clusters on at least one major cloud
• Hands-on with Terraform / OpenTofu and GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux)
• Has built security automation, not only operated tools: policy-as-code, secrets rotation, CI/CD security gates or detection pipelines
• Working knowledge of IAM, network security, TLS and secrets management across clouds
• Scripting and tooling in Python or Go
• Has been through security audits and knows what evidence auditors need
• Has built or used AI-based automation in infrastructure or security work, and understands the risks of AI agents: prompt injection, over-broad permissions, unreviewed actions
• Nice to have: Vault, SPIFFE / SPIRE, Falco or Tetragon, Cloudflare WAF, incident response lead experience, multi-cloud experience

fcbe6bafd61d7005.description: **About Metaforms** Metaforms is a vertically integrated AI SaaS platform for market research agencies around the world. The platform helps agencies improve speed, consistency, and delivery quality across research workflows that have historically depended on repetitive manual effort and hard-to-scale specialist knowledge. The product surface is unusual. Surveys behave like programs, business workflows contain hidden operational nuance, and a small mistake can create real downstream cost for an agency and its clients. That means product thinking here is not about copying familiar SaaS patterns. It is about understanding how work is actually done, identifying where AI agents can reliably help, and shaping systems that feel intuitive to users while introducing genuinely new workflows underneath. **The Role** You'll be paired with a senior product manager and work closely with senior engineers on a live, shipping product area. Think of this as a structured apprenticeship into product management: you'll take on real pieces of the work sitting in on user calls, drafting write-ups, helping think through a feature with a senior PM reviewing, coaching, and gradually handing you more rope as you show you're ready for it. This role is for someone early in their career who is curious, organized, and eager to learn how product decisions actually get made, not someone expected to already operate independently in ambiguity. You'll be given scoped pieces of larger problems, not owning full ambiguity solo. **What You'll Do** • Sit in on user interviews with research operators, project managers, and agency leaders and take the lead on some, once you're ready to learn how work actually happens. • Start recognizing the difference between what a user asks for and the real problem underneath, with coaching. • Help write up product ideas, user flows, and simple requirements docs for a senior PM to review and refine. • Take a first pass at breaking a defined problem into smaller, engineering-sized pieces, with guidance. • Help build and test simple prototypes or mockups to get early feedback from users and the team. • Sit in on engineering discussions to learn how requirements turn into shipped software. • Answer engineers' clarifying questions on the pieces of work you own, escalating to your senior PM when you're unsure. • Track the status of the features you're closest to and flag blockers early. • Help gather feedback after something ships from users, from support tickets, from usage data and summarize what you find. • Notice when something isn't working as intended and bring it to your senior PM rather than being expected to fix it solo. **What We're Looking For** Must Have - 2-3 years of full-time experience, or strong internship experience, in a business, technical, or analytical role product management background is a plus but not required. - You’re curious about AI beyond prompting. You’ve tinkered with something hands-on, like a side project, an automation, or a small tool built with AI APIs or no-code agents, in class, at work, or just for fun - With strong written communication you can summarize a conversation or a problem clearly and simply. - Genuine curiosity about how software products get built, and comfort asking questions when you don't understand something. - Comfort talking to people outside your own function (users, engineers, designers) and taking good notes from those conversations. - Basic organizational skills you can track a few moving pieces of work and follow up without things falling through the cracks. - Coachability: you're looking for regular feedback and want a senior PM actively shaping your growth, not a fully independent role. Nice to Have • Any prior exposure to B2B software, workflow tools, or AI products. • Familiarity with tools like Figma, Notion, or basic SQL not required, easy to pick up on the job. **Why Metaforms** - A real apprenticeship into product management close mentorship from senior PMs and senior engineers, not a sink-or-swim first job. - Work on AI products that operate in real production environments, not demos or feature theater. - Join a team where product, engineering, and domain understanding are tightly coupled. - Visible, real work from day one your notes, write-ups, and small feature areas genuinely shape what gets built. - Join a Series A funded company at the steepest part of its growth curve.
